chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I guarantee that the one who names (Bismillah) over his food will not complain from it.' So Ibn al-Kawwa said to him: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! I ate a meal yesterday, I named over it, and it harmed me.' He said: 'Perhaps you ate various types, so you named over some of it and did not name over some, O dimwit!'

key_terms.لُكَعُ: Dimwit/fool (term of endearment or mild rebuke)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the guarantee that named food will not cause harm?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the precise conditions for the spiritual protection promised by Ali (peace be upon him) regarding food, highlighting the importance of intentionality and completeness in ritual recitation. The Imam’s witty rebuke of Ibn al-Kawwa underscores a key Shia scholarly principle: divine guarantees are contingent upon the faithful adhering strictly to the prescribed acts, such as ensuring the Bismillah is recited over every component of a mixed meal to prevent specific ailments.
